items.summary: Recommendation: reject new change requests and requeues this cycle. The CRO SEO, UX, performance, affiliate, and repository leads are useful but blocked by existing failure-containment requirements: documented ownership, root cause, deduplication, deterministic validation, rollback, and measurement readiness. Preserve them as deferred backlog; continue current repair-or-close work only.

Approve containment-only execution. No new change requests, requeues, deployments, experiments, dependencies, telemetry, spending, or monetization changes are queue-eligible. Retain SEO, UX, performance, content, accessibility, affiliate, and repository opportunities as deferred backlog until ownership, root cause, deduplication, isolated deterministic validation, rollback, and measurement readiness are documented. Continue only existing repair-or-close, attribution reconciliation, and bounded legal/security evidence work.

Technical feasibility is not the blocker for the deferred opportunities; safe queue entry is. Existing failures and incomplete release evidence require isolated validation and rollback evidence before any implementation or requeue. Use existing recorded telemetry only and preserve all launch gates and parked-site dispositions.

Maintain the private launch gate and unsent external outreach. Continue the existing rights, data-flow, consent, vendor, retention, accuracy, attribution, measurement, and security evidence work only. No public exposure, rights-dependent monetization, alert expansion, credential or configuration change, dependency addition, or deployment is supported.
